title: How build.py turns a spec into this page
subtitle: The example spec this repository ships with: the skill explaining itself. Run it with `python3 skills/code-walkthrough/scripts/build.py examples/self-walkthrough.json`.

flows.who: Claude, after writing the spec · or you, by hand
flows.lead: The spec holds anchors and notes only. The script reads every referenced file from disk, asks git which lines changed, and writes one self-contained HTML page.
alts: Every anchor that did not resolve, listed at once
Source files that changed since the previous build
msgs: find anchor text in the file

panels.role: The whole renderer: one file, standard library only.
notes: Entry point. Merges the built-in UI labels with the spec's own.
Reads a source file and turns each note's anchor into a line number.
hits = [i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(src) if find in l]
A text anchor is a substring match; `[text, n]` picks the n-th hit.
Asks the file's own git repository, so a model class in a sibling repo gets its markers too.
Walks the `-U0` diff: hunk headers give the added lines, `-` lines keep the old text for the hover preview.
Draws the numbered sequence diagram from two short arrays.
Writes the page, then a manifest of file hashes used to report changed sources next time.
